label: Welcome
title: Your Orcacode field manual
lede: Orcacode is the interactive terminal host for Orca Harness. It works inside a chosen workspace, asks before gated actions by default, and keeps your work as a recoverable session.

label: Install & run
title: Start in your workspace
lede: Run Orcacode from the workspace where you want its file tools to operate. It defaults to a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint when no API key is set.

label: Approvals
title: Approve every action
lede: Approvals make the tool call visible before it runs. They are designed for the moment a model moves from explanation to local action.

label: Plan mode
title: Investigate, then plan
lede: Plan mode is a read-only stance for exploration and design. It does not try to guess whether a shell command is safe; it allows only a small, explicit set of research tools.

label: Auto mode
title: Proceed without repeated prompts
lede: Auto mode lets known-safe tools and guarded workspace edits run immediately, then reviews actions that still carry meaningful scope or safety risk.

label: Providers & models
title: Choose a provider and model
lede: Orcacode supports local OpenAI-compatible servers, OpenAI API, OpenRouter, and the OpenAI Codex provider for a ChatGPT subscription.

label: Workspace tools
title: Tools stay in your workspace
lede: The default toolset gives an agent useful local capabilities while rejecting absolute paths and attempts to escape upward from the workspace root.

label: Tools & extensions
title: Tools available now
lede: This is the current Orcacode capability set—not a generic harness API list. Availability depends on session mode, optional configuration, and whether you are in the interactive terminal or a headless run.

label: Memory
title: Remember deliberately
lede: Orcacode keeps deliberate user-owned memory in one local SQLite database, recalls matching global and workspace records automatically, and asks before changing them.

label: Sessions & controls
title: Keep the thread. Branch safely.
lede: Sessions are recorded per workspace as append-only JSONL, so routine exploration remains resumable without asking you to manage transcript files by hand.

label: Subagents
title: Delegate bounded work
lede: A subagent is an independent worker with its own context, loop, and tools. Use it for one clearly defined result—not as a second copy of the entire conversation.

label: MCP servers
title: Connect MCP servers
lede: MCP servers add tools, resources, and prompts through a stdio process. Orcacode keeps discovery separate from schema selection so a large server catalog stays manageable.

label: Plugins
title: Package portable local tools
lede: Agent Plugins 1.0 packages an MCP-over-stdio server with portable metadata. Orcacode links a reviewed local package, keeps it disabled until enabled, and routes its tools through the existing MCP policy path.

label: Skills & instructions
title: Add durable guidance
lede: Instructions give every session the project context it needs. Skills package focused procedures that you can discover, enable, or disable when they apply.

label: Rust SDK
title: Embed Orca Harness in Rust
lede: The orca-harness-sdk crate is a CLI-independent facade for composing models, tools, extensions, sessions, memory, skills, MCP, events, cancellation, and long-context recovery in your own Rust host.

label: First agent
title: Build your first SDK agent
lede: Configure a model, expose only the tools your host intends to authorize, observe a run, and choose the right session lifetime.

label: Host assembly
title: Compose a production SDK host
lede: Combine policy, memory, skills, MCP, processes, subagents, workflows, retries, truncation, and verifiable outcomes behind explicit host-owned boundaries.

label: Background lifecycle
title: Drive background work safely
lede: Distinguish parent runs from session-owned work, reconcile lossy notifications with durable state, continue completed work, and shut down with a bound.

label: Headless runs
title: Run one prompt
lede: Headless mode is for scripts and CI-like workflows where you want a single invocation instead of an interactive terminal session.

label: Architecture
title: A narrow execution kernel
lede: Orca Harness owns the short path from a model response to correctly ordered tool results. Orcacode is the composition layer that turns that kernel into a local terminal agent.

label: Design philosophy
title: Keep the loop small
lede: The project is built around one constraint: the execution path that can act on a machine should stay understandable, measurable, and difficult to accidentally widen.

label: Performance & benchmarks
title: Measure useful work
lede: The benchmark tree separates harness overhead, host startup, deterministic MCP retrieval, fake-subagent stress, and cross-product comparison. Kernel and startup are regression-gated; the other suites are evidence with explicit limits.

label: Troubleshooting
title: Find the blocked layer
lede: Most setup issues are resolved by identifying which layer is refusing the work: the provider connection, the workspace guard, or a deliberate safety policy.
